Tidy and Glance Methods for Fits, Calibrations and Plasma Diagnostics

Source: R/tidy.R
specproc-tidy.Rd

tidy() summarizes the estimates of a fit, a calibration or a plasma diagnostic in a tibble, one row per estimate, and glance() summarizes the fit in a one-row tibble, following the conventions of the broom package. The tibbles of several spectra or samples can then be bound together.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'specproc_peak_fit'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_peak_fit'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_calibration'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_calibration'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_wavelength_calibration'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_wavelength_calibration'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_slope_bias'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_slope_bias'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_boltzmann'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_boltzmann'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_cflibs'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_cflibs'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_uncertainty'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_uncertainty'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_curve_of_growth'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'specproc_curve_of_growth'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A peak fit, or an object returned by calibration_curve(), wavelength_calibration(), slope_bias(), boltzmann(), saha_boltzmann(), cf_libs(), plasma_uncertainty() or curve_of_growth().

conf.int

A logical: add the confidence interval (FALSE, default).

conf.level

The confidence level of the interval. Default is 0.95.

...

Not used.

Value

A tibble.

Details

tidy() returns the columns term, estimate and std.error, with the statistic and p.value of a t test where one applies, and, with conf.int = TRUE, the bounds conf.low and conf.high of the confidence interval at conf.level:

  • a peak fit (an element of the fit column of peak_fit() or multipeak_fit()): the parameters of each line and the common shifts, as in tidied; the test is that of a zero value;

  • calibration_curve(): the intercept, slope and quadratic term, with the test of a zero value;

  • wavelength_calibration(): the coefficients of the polynomial correction of each segment, in powers of the wavelength minus the center of the segment (nm), without standard errors;

  • slope_bias(): the bias and slope, with the test of no correction (a bias of 0, a slope of 1);

  • boltzmann() and saha_boltzmann(): the temperature (K) and the intercept of the plot; the interval of the temperature is that of the slope, transformed, so it is not symmetric (its upper bound is infinite when the interval of the slope reaches zero);

  • cf_libs(): the temperature (with an interval as above), and the atomic_fraction and mass_fraction of each element, without standard errors (see plasma_uncertainty());

  • plasma_uncertainty(): the same quantities with their Monte Carlo standard uncertainties, and always their intervals, at the level of the object;

  • curve_of_growth(): the column density of each species (term), with its number of lines (n.lines) and its largest optical depth (max.optical.depth).

glance() returns:

  • a peak fit: sigma, the root mean square error rmse, isConv, finTol, logLik, AIC, BIC, deviance, df.residual and nobs, as for nls fits in broom (with rmse);

  • calibration_curve(): nobs, r.squared, sigma, df.residual, the sensitivity, the critical.value (ISO 11843 only), lod, loq, the reduced chi.squared of a Deming or York fit, the p-values of Mandel's test (mandel.p.value) and of the lack-of-fit test (lack.of.fit.p.value), the regression and the model;

  • wavelength_calibration(): the number of reference lines n.lines, of lines used nobs, of n.segments, the degree, and the rmse and largest absolute residual max.residual of the lines used (nm);

  • slope_bias(): nobs, the root mean square differences to the reference before (rmse.before) and after (rmse.after) the correction, and whether the slope was fitted (slope.fitted);

  • boltzmann() and saha_boltzmann(): r.squared, sigma, nobs, df.residual, the range of the abscissa energy.range (eV), the electron.density and number of iterations (Saha-Boltzmann only), the method and the units;

  • cf_libs(): r.squared (about the mean), sigma, nobs, df.residual (NA when the temperature is given), the numbers of n.species and n.elements, the electron.density, the number of iterations, the method and the units;

  • plasma_uncertainty(): the number of draws n.draws, of failed draws, the reduced chi.squared of the fit, the level and the method;

  • curve_of_growth(): the temperature, the rmse of the fit (on the log scale), nobs, the scale and the units.

See also

specproc-tidy-models for the chemometric models, peak_fit(), calibration_curve(), boltzmann(), cf_libs(), plasma_uncertainty()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

data(forageLIBS)
mean_spectrum <- colMeans(forageLIBS[-(1:14)])
atomic <- data.frame(
  species = c(rep("Ca I", 6), rep("Ca II", 4)),
  stage = c(rep(1, 6), rep(2, 4)),
  wavelength = c(428.301, 430.253, 431.865, 445.478, 612.222, 616.217,
                 315.887, 317.933, 370.603, 373.690),
  Aki = c(4.34e7, 1.36e8, 7.40e7, 8.70e7, 2.87e7, 4.77e7, 3.10e8, 3.60e8, 8.80e7, 1.70e8),
  gk = c(5, 5, 3, 7, 3, 3, 4, 6, 2, 2),
  Ek = c(4.780, 4.780, 4.769, 4.681, 3.910, 3.910, 7.047, 7.050, 6.468, 6.468)
)
lines <- line_intensities(mean_spectrum, atomic, baseline = TRUE)
fit <- saha_boltzmann(lines, ionization_energy = 6.113, electron_density = 1.9e17)
tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   term        estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>   <chr>          <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
#> 1 temperature 8092.      124.    7815.    8389.    
#> 2 intercept     -0.500     0.195   -0.950   -0.0505
glance(fit)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 9
#>   r.squared sigma  nobs df.residual energy.range electron.density iterations
#>       <dbl> <dbl> <int>       <int>        <dbl>            <dbl>      <int>
#> 1     0.998 0.288    10           8         9.25           1.9e17         10
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: method <chr>, units <chr>

# the K I 769.90 nm line, normalized to the C I 247.86 nm line of the matrix
k <- line_intensities(forageLIBS[-(1:14)], c(C = 247.856, K = 769.896), baseline = TRUE)
standards <- data.frame(K = forageLIBS$K,
                        signal = k$intensity[k$line == "K"] / k$intensity[k$line == "C"])
cal <- calibration_curve(standards, signal, K)
tidy(cal)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   term      estimate std.error statistic  p.value
#>   <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 intercept    0.257    0.0280      9.17 3.58e-18
#> 2 slope        0.144    0.0132     10.9  3.16e-24
glance(cal)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 13
#>    nobs r.squared sigma df.residual sensitivity critical.value   lod   loq
#>   <int>     <dbl> <dbl>       <int>       <dbl>          <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1   368     0.246 0.135         366       0.144             NA  3.09  9.36
#> # ℹ 5 more variables: chi.squared <dbl>, mandel.p.value <dbl>,
#> #   lack.of.fit.p.value <dbl>, regression <chr>, model <chr>
